required_fixes: Frozen decision rule requires BOTH |r| < 0.3 AND permutation p < 0.05 for C3_orthogonality PASS. The observed |r|=0.0527 < 0.3 passes the magnitude threshold, but permutation p=0.414 > 0.05 fails the significance threshold. This is an underpowered confirmatory test (n=240) for very low correlations, not evidence of non-orthogonality. To resolve: either increase sample size (n>=480 recommended for power at |r|~0.05) or revise the frozen decision rule's permutation p threshold for low-magnitude correlations.

The arbitrary session_status_check mapping (401->1.0, 403->0.5, 500->0.75) should be justified or tested for sensitivity. Different mappings could alter the behavioral composite distribution and correlation structure.

Noise-only sample size is 120 (4 conditions x 30), not 240 as originally specified in earlier parent experiments. While FP=0.0 replicates, the smaller n reduces precision of the null control estimate.
validity_findings: TP/variance trade-off IS broken: C1_drift_tp PASS (mean TP=1.0, all Wilson lower CI=0.8865 > 0.75) and C2_variance PASS (8/8 conditions with std>0 for both signals). The design fix from parent (ALL sessions invalid + graded session_status_check) successfully preserves detection while creating variance.

C3_orthogonality FAILs on the frozen decision rule: |r|=0.0527 < 0.3 passes magnitude gate but permutation p=0.414 > 0.05 fails significance gate. This is a known limitation — with true |r|~0.05 and n=240, the permutation test has very low power to achieve p<0.05. The correlation is near-zero (r²=0.003, behavioral explains 0.3% of structural variance).

Positive controls verified: PC_PERMISSION_BOUNDARY_DETECTION rate=1.0 (30/30), PC_SESSION_STATUS_VARIANCE = 4/4 session_invalidation conditions with behavioral std>0. Null control C4_null_control verified: FP=0.0 on 120 noise-only samples.
Measurement validity CONFIRMED: 8/8 co-occurring conditions have within-condition variance for both signals, 240 paired samples available. All validity gates pass.

Session_status_check distribution across {401, 403, 500} is approximately uniform per condition (9-12 each), confirming the graded intensity mechanism operates as designed. No 200 codes appear in SI conditions (session_change=1 always).

Per-drift-pattern correlations: permission_boundary r=0.0514 (n=120), session_invalidation r=0.0462 (n=120). Both very low, consistent with parent's PB-only finding (r=0.051, p=0.577). The pooled r=0.0527 is not driven by session_invalidation as in parent (where SI r=0.189).

Arbitrary session_status_check mapping is a validity threat: the mapping 401->1.0, 403->0.5, 500->0.75 is not grounded in real API behavior and could affect correlation structure. However, ANY mapping that creates variance while keeping session_change=1 tests the core hypothesis (variance without TP dilution).

Deterministic mock server limits external validity: Flask 3.x + PyJWT HS256 on localhost does not capture real API stochasticity (DB/cache/CDN, heterogeneous clients, OAuth/OIDC middleware). Claim ceiling bounded to deterministic mock.
baseline_findings: Parent EXP-GRAPH-35237975537 C1 FAIL (mean TP=0.729) was caused by 50/50 coin flip mixing valid sessions (behavioral=0) into drift labels. This experiment's fix (ALL invalid + graded status) achieves mean TP=1.0 — confirming the audit's root cause analysis (V1_C1_FAIL_BY_DESIGN_ARTIFACT).

Parent pooled |r|=0.1387 (p=0.031) was heterogeneous: PB r=0.051 (p=0.577) vs SI r=0.189 (p=0.038). This experiment's pooled r=0.0527 is homogeneous and low for both drift patterns, eliminating the SI-driven correlation artifact from the bimodal coin-flip design.

Permission_boundary-only orthogonality (r=0.051, p=0.577) replicates across EXP-GRAPH-35191029030, EXP-GRAPH-35237975537, and this experiment — stable finding that PB behavioral and structural signals are near-orthogonal but confirmatory test underpowered.
Null control FP=0.0 on 120 noise-only samples replicates across all three experiments. Behavioral signals do not false-positive on structural noise without drift.
claim_ceiling: Graded session_status_check intensity (401/403/500) while keeping session_change=1 for all session_invalidation samples successfully breaks the TP/variance trade-off: C1_drift_tp PASS (TP=1.0, Wilson lower 0.886) and C2_variance PASS (8/8 conditions with std>0). Behavioral and structural signals show near-orthogonality (|r|=0.053, r²=0.003) but the frozen confirmatory test is underpowered (permutation p=0.414 > 0.05 at n=240). Maximum justified claim: 'Session_invalidation behavioral variance can be achieved without TP dilution using graded status codes; behavioral-structural orthogonality is plausible but not formally confirmed at p<0.05.' Product consequence: architecture should use composite multi-signal classifiers as precautionary measure, not independent parallel channels.
